meta.title: Russia Plague Watch
meta.description: Independent, sourced tracker of the suspected plague case in Irkutsk, Siberia: live incubation countdown, case counts, WHO risk level, claim check and a dated timeline.
meta.disclaimer: This tracker summarises public reporting and official statements. Facts are still disputed, and Russian authorities have not confirmed plague. It is not medical advice. If you have fever and cough after possible exposure, contact a doctor.

headline: WHO says it cannot yet complete a full risk assessment and is waiting for Russia to name the pathogen. Russia says no plague found.

status.label: Suspected, unconfirmed
status.summary: A 28-year-old worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died overnight on 1–2 October after severe pneumonia. Media reports link the death to pneumonic plague. Russian authorities list the cause as "pneumonia of unknown etiology". On 6 October Russia told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested. On 7 October WHO said it was still waiting for Russia to identify the pathogen and could not yet complete a full risk assessment.

watch.label: Incubation watch
watch.explainer: WHO puts plague incubation at 1–7 days. Contacts were last exposed on or before 2 October. If none fall ill by the end of this window, onward spread from this case becomes very unlikely.
watch.closedNote: The window has closed with no symptomatic contacts reported.

claims.claim: The worker died of pneumonic plague
claims.detail: Media reports cite unnamed sources. Russian authorities list pneumonia of unknown etiology. WHO says no cause has been officially confirmed.

claims.claim: She broke a test tube of plague bacteria on 25 September
claims.detail: Reported by the Siberian outlet Lyudi Baikala. Russian officials deny any lab accident.

claims.claim: Plague has spread to her contacts
claims.detail: Russia told WHO on 6 October that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms.

claims.claim: Shelekhov District Hospital was put under quarantine
claims.detail: Announced by Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev on 2 October. Restrictions remain in place.

claims.claim: Russia has shared information with WHO
claims.detail: Russian authorities briefed WHO on 6 October, according to WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier.

claims.claim: There is a second plague case
claims.detail: Media have reported a second institute employee with pneumonia, and some outlets reported a second death. Russian officials have confirmed neither, and the Kremlin calls most media reports on the case false. WHO has asked Russia to clarify reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause.

positions.text: Cause of death is "pneumonia of unknown etiology". Lab analysis found no microorganisms linked to her work with dangerous pathogens. As of 7 October, medical monitoring was complete for over 90% of contacts and nearly 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens. Situation in the region is stable.
Governor Igor Kobzev first cited a suspected "particularly dangerous infection". A special commission later named the cause "pneumonia of unknown aetiology".

WHO says it cannot yet conduct a full risk assessment and has asked Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia. Its initial assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe.
Reports cite sources saying the worker broke a test tube containing Yersinia pestis on 25 September and was infected with pneumonic plague.
Spokesman Dmitry Peskov says the overwhelming majority of media reporting on the case is false and points to Rospotrebnadzor's statements. He says no call with President Trump has been arranged yet.

timeline.title: Plague bacterium isolated on the Russia–Mongolia border
timeline.body: Joint Russian and Mongolian teams isolate a Yersinia pestis culture near Sagaan-Uul, confirming high activity in the Sailyugem natural plague focus. Rospotrebnadzor says there is no direct threat to people.

timeline.title: Test tube reportedly broken in the lab
timeline.body: According to media reports, the worker broke a test tube containing Yersinia pestis while handling live samples. Russian officials deny a lab accident.

timeline.title: Worker hospitalised with severe pneumonia
timeline.body: The 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East is admitted to hospital in Shelekhov.

timeline.title: Death confirmed; Shelekhov hospital quarantined
timeline.body: She dies overnight on 1–2 October. Governor Igor Kobzev cites a suspected "particularly dangerous infection". Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova flies in for an emergency commission. 197 contacts are identified and 189 hospitalised for observation. Kobzev says none have symptoms and all tests are negative.

timeline.title: Rospotrebnadzor: "pneumonia of unknown etiology"
timeline.body: The agency says the situation is stable, lab analysis found no pathogen linked to her work, and daily testing of contacts found only 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases.

timeline.title: WHO in contact with Moscow; White House monitoring
timeline.body: WHO says it is working to verify the event and that risk to the general population appears low. The White House says it is monitoring reports of a suspected case.

timeline.title: EU monitoring "very closely"; US offers help
timeline.body: The European Commission says it is ready to coordinate a response among member states if needed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says it is "not cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus". President Trump says the US is "willing to help".

timeline.title: Regional commission repeats "unknown aetiology" finding
timeline.body: Officials say the health situation in Irkutsk Oblast is stable. Quarantine measures at the Shelekhov hospital remain in place.

timeline.title: No plague found in contacts tested so far
timeline.body: Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.

timeline.title: Russia tells WHO no plague found in contacts; WHO rates the risk
timeline.body: Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.

timeline.title: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
timeline.body: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.

timeline.title: Rospotrebnadzor: monitoring complete for over 90% of contacts
timeline.body: Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".

timeline.title: Kremlin calls most media reports false; second-case reports unconfirmed
timeline.body: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "the vast majority" of media reporting on the situation is false information and urged people to rely on Rospotrebnadzor's statements. Media have reported a second institute employee with pneumonia, and some outlets a second death; Russian officials have confirmed neither. WHO has asked Russia to clarify the reports.

timeline.title: US asks Russia for more information; Putin call not yet arranged
timeline.body: A State Department spokesperson said the US has officially requested additional information from the Russian government. President Trump has said he plans to speak with President Putin about the case. The Kremlin said on 7 October that no call had been arranged yet but that it was open to one.

history.text: Human bubonic case in Kosh-Agach district, Altai Republic, linked to a marmot.
Human bubonic case in Altai after dressing a marmot caught in the Elangash valley.
A 10-year-old boy in Kosh-Agach catches bubonic plague skinning a marmot. 17 contacts quarantined; he survives.
Sailyugem area on the Mongolian border shows high activity. In October, the suspected Irkutsk lab case.

facts.a: Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The pneumonic form infects the lungs and is the only form that spreads person to person, through respiratory droplets. WHO says untreated pneumonic plague can kill within 18–24 hours of onset.
Yes. Common antibiotics such as streptomycin, gentamicin, doxycycline and ciprofloxacin work if started early. Close contacts are usually given preventive antibiotics.
Sudden fever, chills, headache, weakness, then fast-developing pneumonia with chest pain, cough and sometimes bloody sputum.
WHO gives 1–7 days. Pneumonic plague can appear in as little as 24 hours.

Russia has 11 natural plague foci, mostly in the steppes and mountains of the south and Siberia. Rodents and their fleas carry it. Human cases are rare; the last reported were in the Altai Republic in 2014–2016.

card.title: Suspected plague death in Siberia
card.sub: A lab worker in Irkutsk Oblast died of pneumonia on 1–2 Oct. Plague is not confirmed. WHO is waiting for Russia to name the pathogen.
